editorial_guidance.audience: People who love games; no technical background assumed.
editorial_guidance.rule: No game-design or development terminology in reader-facing text, headings, captions, contents, credits or metadata.
editorial_guidance.keep_internal: Build IDs, implementation status, technical art specifications and process notes belong in manifests and README only.
editorial_guidance.qualifications: Picture captions should describe the subject, action, atmosphere or useful player information. Do not discuss development history, earlier versions, prototype status or production progress. Keep asset provenance and development qualifications in internal records only. Remove tentative preview-artwork and exploring-an-idea captions. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable. Actual missing editorial content uses conspicuous TODOs.
editorial_guidance.preserve: Approved profiles and lore, spoiler-free policy and current names. Do not imply unfinished encounters are playable.
editorial_guidance.writing_style: Follow AGENTS.md Writing Style: Avoid Formulaic AI Copy. Use natural, varied sentences and specific observations. Avoid repeated paired fragments, formulaic contrasts and generic trailer language. Review all creative copy for repetitive rhetorical patterns before publication.
editorial_guidance.corporate_horror: Imply the Spare Employee Dispenser's disturbing practices through corporate euphemisms and omissions. Do not disclose its lethal mechanism or describe bodily processing. Never refer to the viewer's screen or other fourth-wall-breaking presentation details in magazine copy.
editorial_guidance.pending_revision: Edition 22 adds Gratecrawler and approved Sputtervalve using existing sprite artwork and descriptive copy. Only Gratecrawler remains a working name; origin lore pending for both. Clogfather stays descriptive only.
editorial_guidance.todos: Actual unresolved editorial placeholders must say TODO: followed by the specific missing item. Use a conspicuous high-contrast box with bold type at least 18 pt, with sufficient space and no clipping. Never bury TODOs in small italic captions or replace them with vague caveats. Do not invent TODOs for existing artwork merely because gameplay is unfinished.
editorial_guidance.clogfather_revision: First description preserved; redundant paragraph and idle inset replaced with Tony horror reaction.
editorial_guidance.disclaimers: Do not add fictional-company, fictional-publication or non-affiliation disclaimers to reader-facing magazine content.
editorial_guidance.creature_order: Five non-bosses first, then Skitterling miniboss, then Clogfather. No current playability claim for unintegrated encounters.
editorial_guidance.skitterling: Skitterling is the official name, explicitly confirmed by Sean on 2026-10-17, unless he changes it. No working-name label. Existing conceptual art, no origin lore or fight-solution claims.
editorial_guidance.costume_surprises: Only normal-costume portraits, sprites and gameplay images. Never reveal Easy or Hard costumes or describe them in reader copy.
editorial_guidance.weapon_previews: Two hero pages pair default weapons with approved named specials. Four future weapons retain silhouettes and tentative names; SPECIAL / ??? means no approved special exists. These are intentional teasers, not missing copy or promises. Backpack jetter action illustration is concept art, not a runtime claim.
editorial_guidance.torch_teaser: Sean approved inclusion of the optional soldering torch as a tentative magazine teaser on November 5. This does not approve implementation, ownership or a named special. Grouped on Tony page as an idea, not an exclusive character assignment.
editorial_guidance.review_status: Edition 39 draft authorized for publication by Sean on 2026-11-14 for remote feedback; independent Art review and cover/back-cover likeness corrections remain pending.
editorial_guidance.main_break: Implemented in Prototype183 per Engineering; use corrected geyser/rain conceptv2. Rain lasts7.5seconds after cinematic. Illustration remains concept art.

elements.text: DRAIN DAMAGE / THE GAME GUIDE / EDITION 39
Meet the crew, inspect the creatures and find out what waits beyond the basement.
TOOLS & SPECIALS  04    /    FIELD GUIDE  06    /    DOWN THE DRAIN  08
LAYOUT REVIEW / SEAN LIKENESS CORRECTION PENDING
A guide to the people, equipment and unpleasant surprises of Drain Damage.
Tony knows the trade. Sean is learning it. Their employer has sent them into a basement where the plumbing has started causing trouble of its own.
This issue introduces the game through its crew, creatures and places. You can browse the pictures or settle into the articles; the important surprises stay in the game.
Begin with the crew, then look through their tools before heading downstairs. Later, the job takes a very wet turn. The equipment preview at the back is a look at possibilities, with tentative names.
Tony and Sean, before the trouble starts.
Starting weapons and their special abilities.
Creature lore, behavior and a few things to watch.
The Flush, its contents and an unusual ride.
Five possible additions to the tool shed.
Tony is teaching Sean a trade that keeps getting stranger.

Tony comes from four generations of plumbers and has spent decades installing, building and keeping essential systems running. He takes the work seriously and makes time to teach Sean properly. A difficult job won't put him off. A large spider might slow him down a little.
Plumbing runs in the family. Tony brings that knowledge to each job, along with the patience to explain what he's doing. Sean has a great deal to learn, and Tony intends to give him the chance.
Sean wandered in looking for work and somehow ended up on Tony's crew. He's willing to help, although it's worth checking what he's holding before asking him to hand you a tool.
Sean arrived without much knowledge of plumbing. Tony took him on anyway. For now, enthusiasm is doing a lot of the work, and a patient teacher is keeping the rest moving.
NEXT: WHAT THEY BRING TO WORK  /  TOOLS & SPECIALS
The starting kit and the special that changes the job.
Tony starts with a compact pressure gun that fires quick water shots. Keep a steady aim when the creatures close in.
A thick water jet keeps blasting while the recoil pushes Tony backward. Keep room behind you when you open the nozzle.
Two special uses per level. Save one for the moment you need room most.
The starting kit and the special that changes the job.
Sean starts with a hefty launcher that fires rubber plungers. The shots hit hard, but leave yourself room between them.
Sean hauls a huge pipe from the floor. A geyser shoots upward, then rain falls across the screen for 7.5 seconds. It hits enemies once a second while Sean can move and fire.
Two special uses per level. Save one for the moment you need room most.
CREATURES / RECOGNIZE THE TROUBLE BEFORE IT REACHES YOU

This bad-tempered fixture has burning red eyes under a lid-like brow, ceramic teeth around its bowl, and short pipe legs. It patrols until a plumber gets too close, then closes the distance with a hop. The service appointment is unlikely to go as planned.
Look for pipe legs, red eyes and teeth around the bowl. When it begins following you, leave room for its next hop.
Flushfiend: porcelain chips away until the fixture comes apart.

For years, the worst thing about a basement spider was losing sight of it. Then one sprouted wings and apparently started breeding. The Hallowed Widow is a huge, hairy nightmare with ivory fangs, white feathers, and a golden halo - every reassuring detail attached to the wrong animal. Early witnesses watched the floor. Later witnesses learned to watch the ceiling, too. Nobody knows where the wings came from. Religious and non-religious people alike have expressed concerns about what this implies for heaven.
Watch the Widow: It dives, rises and pauses above you before turning for another pass.

A rusty drain strainer sits in this sludge creature’s back, above a mouth full of porcelain teeth. It climbs from a grate and patrols the floor. Watch its hands: it pauses, faces you and throws a ball of muck before moving on.
Service tip: Move as its hand rises. The muck arcs toward where you were.

That angry face belongs to a pressure valve bolted firmly in place. Its outlet spits violet shots without a charging warning. It cannot follow you, but it can aim at you, so standing in front of it is still a poor idea.
Service tip: Keep moving past the outlet. Don’t wait for a charge warning before dodging.

A maintenance crew found Gnatastrophe circling a blocked vent with the persistence of aircraft waiting for landing clearance. They have since been spotted throughout the sewers, flying in close formation toward no particular destination. Their buzzing carries impressively far for something with so little to report. Plumbers and monsters alike suffer for wandering into their flight path. Nobody has identified a commanding officer, although several flies appear to be taking credit.
The flies drift without hunting. Crossing their path hurts plumbers and monsters alike.

A cockroach crossing the floor is bad enough. Skitterling begins with hundreds, crawling over one another until the heap takes on a shape you recognize. Even then, nothing holds still. Legs and antennae keep moving across its body, and every part of the silhouette is another insect trying to find its place.

A colossal living fatberg of congealed grease, wet wipes, roots, and things nobody should have flushed. Wedged into the collection chamber beneath headquarters, it heaves against the pipework and spits the accumulated consequences back at anyone approaching.
The service call takes an unexpected turn. There is nowhere dry to stand.

The handle has been pulled, and the bowl is rather larger than either plumber expected. The current carries everything somebody thought would fit down a toilet. Keep an eye on the drain while watching for whatever comes down next.
There are no useful tools to reach for here. Swimming will have to do until the current decides where the job goes next. Watch the water for incoming debris and keep clear of the drain.
Once you are riding, the view opens onto a channel of rushing water and plumbing hardware. Look ahead before choosing where to cross. A convenient-looking surface deserves a second glance.
Tony and Sean have survived plenty of unpleasant service calls. Neither packed for this one.

pages.section: Beyond the basement / What came down with you

elements.text: BEYOND THE BASEMENT / WHAT CAME DOWN WITH YOU
Somebody has pulled the handle. The contents have stopped respecting personal space.
Sean has found transport. The company is unlikely to reimburse him. Keep watching the channel ahead; the water and plumbing hardware make an awkward route home.
Corn, keys and everything else circle the same drain. The dead hamster is unlikely to offer much advice.

Billy-Joe runs Mainframe Plumbing & Supply from a beige server rack. Every plumbing company and distribution warehouse in the country answers to him, so asking for a different manager won't get you very far. Tony and Sean get their assignments from his green screen. BJ has plenty of work for them and very little interest in hearing why it might be unpleasant.

BJ speaks calmly, keeps the jobs coming, and expects his employees to get on with them. If you're hoping the smiling face means he's concerned about your welfare, you may want to ask a more specific question.
BJ IS TAKING AN UNWELCOME INTEREST IN YOUR WORK.

Mainframe Plumbing & Supply would like you to know that arrangements have been made. The Spare Employee Dispenser stands ready between service calls, its glass front offering a reassuring view of the company’s preparations. There is rust around the hinges and something familiar about the occupants. The accompanying leaflet describes them as reserve personnel. It asks employees to respect their rest and directs all further questions to the same leaflet.

The leaflet is particularly clear on continuity of service. Your assignments will remain on the schedule, your tools will still be required, and your name will stay on the rota. Several paragraphs explain how much the company values an experienced employee. The section headed “What this means for you” refers back to those paragraphs. We would have preferred a little more detail, but the cabinet does appear to be well stocked.
The company asks that reserve personnel not be disturbed.
Five possible additions to the kit. Names and details are tentative.
A quick swing for close company.
A coiled cable with a little extra reach.
A weighty answer to a stubborn blockage.
Lob a little demolition down the corridor.
LAYOUT REVIEW / SEAN LIKENESS CORRECTION PENDING

design_guidance.format: Content-led editorial issue with expandable article lengths; no fixed page cap. Current review has twelve pages after consolidation, not a limit.
design_guidance.creatures: Seven creatures in two dense pages: five non-bosses before both bosses.
design_guidance.references: User-supplied Nintendo Power / GamePro spreads; layouts reinterpreted with original game artwork.
design_guidance.action_gallery: Asymmetric action study with a dominant Widow image, offset sprite sequences and narrow caption columns.
